characters.description: Chicago's wizard and Warden, enjoying a rare stretch of quiet - which ends when the Queen of Winter comes to collect. Harry still owes Mab two favors from an old bargain, and the one she calls in drops him between the Winter and Summer Courts, the city's underworld, and the return of the worst enemies he has: the Knights of the Blackened Denarius. Something is also subtly wrong with his own magic, a gap he cannot quite see - and working out who arranged that, and why, is part of the game.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The Queen of the Winter Court, holder of two favors Harry has owed since she bought his debt years ago. Mab appears in person to call in the second: Harry will act as her Emissary and protect - of all people - John Marcone. Her motives, as always, are layered beneath centuries of ice; she gives Harry neither reasons nor mercy, and some of her help arrives in forms that look, until the last moment, exactly like sabotage.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: Sergeant Karrin Murphy, Harry's partner in everything the law has no words for. She works the Marcone abduction from the mortal side, walks knowingly into a war between fallen angels and faerie queens, and in the book's darkest hour proves - in a way that surprises everyone, herself included - exactly what kind of person can hold a holy blade.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: Chicago's crime lord - recently become the first ordinary mortal to sign the Unseelie Accords as a freeholding lord, making him a recognized power among the supernatural nations. When he is taken from a fortified panic room by enemies who went through his defenses like paper, his abduction is the small favor of the title: Mab wants him found and protected, and Harry has to swallow years of enmity to do it. Even as a prisoner, Marcone plays a cold, disciplined long game.
characters.name: John Marcone

characters.description: Marcone's security consultant: a tall, blonde, terrifyingly capable woman who is far more than human - a valkyrie on contract from Monoc Securities. Gard's professional loyalty to Marcone survives his abduction, and her knowledge of the powers in play, her runes, and her axe make her one of the most valuable allies in the hunt for her employer.
characters.name: Sigrun Gard

characters.description: Knight of the Cross, bearer of Amoracchius, Harry's oldest ally in the war against the Denarians - and a father and husband whose family has already paid dearly for his calling. When Nicodemus and the coins return, Michael takes the field with his usual unshakable faith. The question that has always hung over the Knights - how far God's protection extends, and what happens when the plan requires a sacrifice - has never pressed harder than it does in this book.
characters.name: Michael Carpenter

characters.description: The agnostic Russian Knight of the Cross, bearer of Esperacchius, cheerful in the face of horrors that would break most soldiers. Sanya arrives to stand with Michael and Harry against the Denarians he once served, bringing his rifle, his good humor, and his firsthand understanding of what the coins do to the people who carry them.
characters.name: Sanya

characters.description: The Archive - the living sum of everything humanity has ever written - still vested in a small, solemn girl whom Harry calls Ivy. Bound to absolute neutrality, she is summoned to preside over a formal parley under the Accords when the Denarian crisis becomes a matter between nations. Her power is oceanic; her situation - one child, neutral, alone, and unique - is precisely the kind of thing an enemy who thinks in millennia knows how to exploit.
characters.name: The Archive

characters.description: The Archive's bodyguard, the mercenary who has kept her alive through everything her office attracts. Kincaid fights the book's battles with his usual meticulous, inhuman competence, and his bond with his young charge - gruff, unsentimental, and absolute - is tested by the worst thing that has ever happened on his watch.
characters.name: Kincaid

characters.description: The two-thousand-year-old leader of the Order of the Blackened Denarius, back in Chicago with his wife Tessa, his daughter Deirdre, and a full muster of coin-bound fallen angels. Nicodemus abducted Marcone as an opening move in a scheme aimed at a far greater prize, and he negotiates, betrays, and murders with the genial patience of a man who has been winning for twenty centuries. The noose at his throat remains one of the few things in creation that can hurt him.
characters.name: Nicodemus Archleone

characters.description: Harry's apprentice, whose subtle magic - veils and senses - now has real polish, and whose greatest contribution to this case is noticing something everyone else missed: a precise, surgical absence in Harry's own behavior. Molly stays largely behind the lines of the book's battles, but her perception changes the course of the endgame.
characters.name: Molly Carpenter

characters.description: A quiet man pushing a mop in a hospital corridor, who turns out to be something else entirely: Uriel, an archangel, appearing to Harry in the aftermath of the book's battles. Softly spoken and precise about the limits of what he may do, he confirms the nature of the new silver-white fire that has crept into Harry's magic, and leaves Harry with the sense that the war he can see is a small corner of a much larger one.
characters.name: Uriel

recaps.ending: The Denarians' true target was never Marcone: the abduction was the opening move of a scheme to capture the Archive, and at the Accords parley they take Ivy after a devastating battle. Harry answers with an assault on the Denarians' island stronghold in Lake Michigan, alongside Michael, Sanya, Murphy, Kincaid and Luccio. Mab returns what she had secretly taken - Harry's blasting rod, veiled from his own memory along with his fire magic - and Harry burns the enemy's position down around them. Ivy and Marcone are recovered alive; a number of Denarians are killed and several of their coins captured; Nicodemus, half-strangled with his own noose, survives through his daughter Deirdre and escapes; Tessa escapes as well. In the battle Murphy takes up the holy sword Fidelacchius, which blazes for her, though she declines its calling. The victory's price is Michael: gunned down during the extraction, he survives only barely and is left too badly maimed to fight again - his sword, Amoracchius, passes into Harry's keeping alongside Fidelacchius, and Michael retires to his family with a serenity Harry cannot fathom. In a hospital corridor the archangel Uriel, wearing a janitor's clothes, confirms what has changed in Harry: the death of Lasciel's shadow left space that has filled with soulfire, Heaven's counterpart to hellfire, fueled by Harry's own soul. Mab's second favor is paid, one remains, Marcone stands as an Accords lord with his debts to Harry unresolved, and Ivy - saved by a wizard who refused to write her off as an office - has a friend for the first time.
recaps.in_short: Mab calls in the second of Harry's three favors: act as Winter's Emissary and protect John Marcone, newly a freeholding lord under the Accords and abducted from a panic room by the returned Knights of the Blackened Denarius. As Summer inexplicably sends its goat-legged gruff assassins after Harry and his own fire magic has somehow gone missing from his mind, Harry hunts Nicodemus through parleys and betrayals - and learns too late that Marcone was bait: the Denarians' real target is the Archive, the little girl Ivy, whom they seize at the Accords negotiation. Harry leads Michael, Sanya, Murphy, Kincaid and Luccio in an assault on the Denarians' island in Lake Michigan; Mab returns his blasting rod and the memory she had veiled, and the stronghold burns. Ivy and Marcone are saved, coins are captured, Nicodemus and Tessa escape - and Michael is shot down in the extraction, crippled out of his knighthood, his sword joining Fidelacchius in Harry's trust. Uriel reveals Harry's new silver fire is soulfire, one Winter favor remains, and Harry finishes the job having beaten the eldest gruff with a donut.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden broke a conspiracy inside the White Court that was murdering Chicago's minor practitioners, clearing his half-brother Thomas and leaving Lara Raith - the true power behind the White King - in his debt, while confirming that a hidden 'Black Council' arms its pawns with Outsider power through agents like the necromancer Cowl. The shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel, which had lived in Harry's mind since he grabbed her coin to save a child, chose to die shielding him, leaving his head silent. Harry trains Molly Carpenter as his apprentice under a shared death sentence; Murphy, demoted for standing with him, still runs his mortal-world flank. Of the three favors Harry once owed Mab, Queen of Winter, two remain. The holy sword Fidelacchius rests in his keeping. His enemies of record include Nicodemus Archleone and the coin-bound fallen angels of the Blackened Denarius - and crime lord John Marcone has just become the first mortal to sign the Unseelie Accords as a freeholding lord.

A snowball fight at the Carpenter home is interrupted by monsters out of a fairy tale: gruffs, the goat-legged soldiers of Summer, attacking Harry with military precision - and each wave that fails is followed by a bigger brother. Before Harry can work out why the Summer Court wants him dead, Winter answers the question's other half: Mab appears and calls in the second of his three favors. John Marcone has been abducted - taken from a fortified safe room by something that tore through his precautions - and Harry, as Winter's Emissary, is to find and protect him. The scene of the abduction shows Denarian handiwork, and Marcone's people, the valkyrie Gard and the enormous Hendricks, join the hunt for their employer. Harry also can't shake the feeling that something small is missing from his own habits, though he cannot name it.

The enemy shows its face: Nicodemus Archleone is back in Chicago with his wife Tessa, his daughter Deirdre, and more coin-bound Denarians than Harry has ever seen in one place - and because Marcone is a signatory of the Accords, his abduction is a matter between nations. A formal parley is convened, with the Archive - Ivy, the solemn little girl who is the sum of human written knowledge - summoned as neutral arbiter, her bodyguard Kincaid at her side. Michael and Sanya, the Knights of the Cross, take the field as the Denarians' oldest enemies. The negotiation at the Shedd Aquarium is a Denarian trap: the parley erupts into battle, and the enemy's design finally shows itself - the fallen angels' interest reaches past Marcone toward something far more valuable.

The aquarium battle costs the Denarians dearly but wins them their true prize: Ivy. The Archive - one small girl, neutral, unique, and irreplaceable - is taken, to be broken or claimed for the coins, and Kincaid is nearly killed failing to prevent it. Amid the wreckage Harry pieces the scheme together: Marcone was bait from the start, the parley a mechanism to bring the Archive within reach. Molly, meanwhile, has spotted the surgical absence in Harry's behavior - he has not used fire magic in weeks, his blasting rod is nowhere in his memory, and he never noticed: someone has been inside his head. Hunted by Summer's gruffs whenever he surfaces, bargaining with powers on every side, Harry locates the Denarians' stronghold - an island far out in Lake Michigan - and Nicodemus offers terms designed to cost Harry his soul either way. Harry chooses assault instead.

The strike force crosses the lake in the teeth of winter: Harry, Michael, Sanya, Murphy, Kincaid and Warden-Captain Luccio, against a fortified island held by fallen angels. In the battle's crux Mab returns what she had taken - the blasting rod, and the veiled memory of his own fire magic - and Harry understands the manipulation only as he turns it loose: his fire, hidden even from himself until the moment it could be decisive, burns the Denarians' position down around them. Ivy is pulled alive out of her captors' hands; Marcone is recovered; Denarians die and coins are taken. Nicodemus, choked with his own noose for the second time in his long life, is saved by Deirdre and escapes with Tessa. And in the extraction, gunfire finds Michael Carpenter, and the best man Harry knows goes down.

The bill comes due, and the accounting is strange. Michael survives - barely - but his body is ruined for war: his knighthood is over, and he accepts it with a peace that baffles Harry, going home to Charity and the children he now gets to grow old with; Amoracchius joins Fidelacchius in Harry's keeping, two swords waiting for bearers. Murphy, who took up Fidelacchius in the island battle and saw it blaze in her hands, declines the calling on her own terms. The eldest gruff, Summer's final and mightiest assassin, is defeated by the letter of faerie law and a donut - Harry's kind of victory. In a hospital corridor, a janitor who is the archangel Uriel confirms what the perceptive have noticed: the space where Lasciel's shadow died has filled with soulfire, the fire of Heaven, drawn from Harry's own soul. Mab's second favor is paid with one remaining; Marcone resumes his throne owing Harry his life; Ivy, guarded by a healing Kincaid, has gained the one thing the Archive was never permitted - a friend. The coins are locked away, but Tessa's escape and the design behind the whole affair promise the Denarians are not finished with Harry Dresden.

characters.description: A large, slow-seeming novice in the great Church of the god Om, in the theocratic nation of Omnia. Illiterate but gifted with a flawless memory that forgets nothing he has seen or heard, he is devout, literal-minded, and unfailingly kind. He tends the Citadel's melon garden, and is startled when a small tortoise begins to speak to him, claiming to be his god.
characters.name: Brutha

characters.description: The Great God Om, worshipped by millions across Omnia, who discovers to his horror that he has been reduced to a nearly powerless one-eyed tortoise. A god's strength depends on the number of people who truly believe in him rather than merely in his Church, and Om finds he has only one real believer left, the novice Brutha, the only person who can hear him. Blustering and self-centred, he must rely on Brutha simply to survive.
characters.name: Om

characters.description: A deacon of the Church and a leading figure in the Quisition, Omnia's feared apparatus for detecting and punishing heresy. Austere, patient, and utterly certain of his own righteousness, he wields terror as an instrument of faith and pursues power within the Church with cold single-mindedness. He takes an interest in Brutha's perfect memory.
characters.name: Vorbis

characters.description: A blind, cynical philosopher of Ephebe who lives in a barrel and carries a lantern, known for a plain-spoken, questioning outlook. He is the author of a book describing the world as a disc carried on the back of a great turtle, a view that is deep heresy in Omnia, which teaches that the world is a sphere.
characters.name: Didactylos

characters.description: The nephew and assistant of the philosopher Didactylos, a young man fascinated by machines and mechanisms. Practical where his uncle is contemplative, he applies philosophy to engineering and builds devices to solve problems.
characters.name: Urn

characters.description: A sergeant in the Omnian army who secretly leads an underground movement against the Church's tyranny. Hardened and angry at the cruelties of the Quisition, he wants to bring the whole oppressive structure down by force.
characters.name: Sergeant Simony

characters.description: An unassuming, elderly sweeper who moves quietly about the Citadel with a broom, easily overlooked and treated as a nobody. He is in fact far more than he appears, a member of an order that watches over the proper unfolding of history, and he keeps a discreet eye on events in Omnia.
characters.name: Lu-Tze

characters.description: The elderly novice-master of the Citadel, in charge of the young men in Brutha's dormitory. Set in his ways and given to muttering at the temptations he imagines everywhere, he oversees Brutha's early religious instruction.
characters.name: Brother Nhumrod

recaps.ending: Small Gods ends with the tyranny of Omnia's Church broken and a new, gentler order begun. At the point of Brutha's public execution, the Great God Om finally reclaims his strength: carried up by an eagle and dropped onto Deacon Vorbis, he kills the man who had seized control of the Church, and as the crowd sees Brutha's courage, true belief floods back to Om. Brutha survives and becomes the new prophet. Instead of wielding the power he inherits as his predecessors did, he strikes a new bargain with his god and remakes Omnia, abolishing the Quisition and steering the nation toward tolerance, literacy, and a lasting peace, while stopping the war Vorbis had provoked. The story then jumps a hundred years forward to Brutha's own death as an old man. When Death comes for him and he must cross the desert that lies beyond life, Brutha finds the spirit of Vorbis still standing there, alone and terrified, unmoved since his death because he had never truly cared for anyone but himself. Brutha takes Vorbis's hand and walks with him across the desert, choosing kindness toward his old enemy as his final act.
recaps.in_short: In the theocratic nation of Omnia, the Great God Om finds his power gone: because true belief, not mere Church membership, feeds a god, and only the kind, perfectly remembering novice Brutha genuinely believes in him, Om has shrunk to a nearly helpless talking tortoise. Brutha, the only one who can hear him, is taken into the service of Deacon Vorbis, a cold master of the Church's torturing Quisition, and travels with him to the philosopher-city of Ephebe, where forbidden ideas, including that the world is a disc on a turtle, begin to shake Brutha's unquestioning faith. Vorbis engineers treachery and war; after a shipwreck Brutha carries the injured Vorbis across the desert out of sheer decency. In Omnia, Vorbis makes himself prophet and condemns Brutha to death, but Om intervenes, dropped by an eagle onto Vorbis to kill him as belief and his power return. Brutha becomes prophet, ends the Quisition, and turns Omnia toward tolerance and peace. A century later, dying, he helps even Vorbis's frightened soul cross the desert of death.

recaps.text: In the theocratic nation of Omnia, whose powerful Church enforces worship of the Great God Om, a slow but kind novice named Brutha, blessed with a perfect memory, is astonished when a small one-eyed tortoise begins speaking to him and claims to be Om himself. Om has discovered a terrible truth: a god's power comes from genuine belief, and though millions attend his Church out of fear and habit, Brutha is the only person left who truly believes in him, which is why he has dwindled to a near-helpless tortoise able to speak to no one else. Brutha's gift for remembering everything draws the notice of Deacon Vorbis, a cold and formidable figure of the Quisition, the Church's machinery of inquisition and torture. Vorbis takes Brutha into his service and includes him in a diplomatic mission to the distant city of Ephebe.

The mission reaches Ephebe, a coastal city of philosophers and argument, utterly unlike rigid Omnia. There Brutha, carrying Om the tortoise with him, encounters thinkers such as the blind, barrel-dwelling philosopher Didactylos and his inventor nephew Urn. He is confronted by ideas forbidden at home, above all the claim that the world is a disc riding on a great turtle, which contradicts the Church's teaching that it is a sphere. Brutha, who has never questioned anything, begins to be troubled by what he learns and by the gap between his Church's cruelty and the god he actually hears. Vorbis, meanwhile, pursues his own designs behind the mission's official purpose.

Vorbis's true intentions surface as he engineers treachery to serve the Church's ambitions, turning the diplomatic errand toward conflict between Omnia and Ephebe. In the upheaval Brutha, Vorbis, and Om flee Ephebe by sea, but their vessel is wrecked and they are cast into the desert. There Brutha, out of simple decency, carries the injured and helpless Vorbis across the burning wasteland on his back, keeping alive the man who embodies everything cruel about his Church. Om, still a vulnerable tortoise dependent on Brutha, is carried along, and Brutha's steady kindness under extremity marks him as something the Church never made him.

Back in Omnia, Vorbis consolidates his power and has himself installed as the Church's new prophet and supreme head, staging events to confirm his authority. Brutha, whose growing conscience and knowledge make him dangerous, is condemned as a heretic and prepared for public execution, to be tortured to death on an iron instrument before the assembled faithful. Om, still nearly powerless, is desperate to save his one believer but can do almost nothing in his tortoise form. The confrontation between Brutha's plain goodness and Vorbis's ruthless certainty comes to a head before the crowds of the Citadel.

At the climax Om finally acts: he arranges to be carried aloft by an eagle and dropped from a great height onto Vorbis, killing him, and as the crowd witnesses Brutha's courage and the god's returning power, real belief surges back and Om is restored to strength. Brutha survives and becomes the new prophet of Omnia. Rather than continue the Church's tyranny, he negotiates a new understanding with Om, ending the Quisition and turning Omnia toward tolerance, learning, and peace, and he halts the war that Vorbis's schemes had set in motion. The book closes many years later: Brutha dies as an old man, and Death comes for him. In the desert that souls must cross, Brutha finds the terrified spirit of Vorbis, who has stood alone and frightened there ever since his death, and takes him by the hand to help him make the journey, returning kindness for cruelty one last time.

characters.description: A gentle, determined girl in the same rigidly controlled community from the start of the series, assigned the role of Birthmother, or Vessel, to produce infants for the society. She is only fourteen when she bears her first child. Unlike others around her, she is not fully numbed to feeling, and she forms a fierce, forbidden attachment to the son she was never meant to know. That love becomes the driving purpose of her life.
characters.name: Claire

characters.description: Claire's infant son, the baby she bears in the controlled community and is forbidden to keep. In that society children are assigned to family units, and this small, restless infant does not thrive on its rigid schedule. He is the child at the center of Claire's search, and the thread that ties her story to the wider world of the series.
characters.name: Gabe

characters.description: A young man, known from earlier in the series, who once fled the controlled community as a boy carrying an infant to safety and later became the wise leader of a welcoming settlement. He is marked by pale eyes and a gift for perception. Claire's search will eventually cross paths with the community he guides.
characters.name: Jonas

characters.description: A young man in a remote, isolated settlement, patient and kind, who helps Claire rebuild her strength and teaches her the difficult skill of climbing the steep cliff that walls the village off from the world beyond. He bears the marks of a hard past of his own and understands, better than most, the danger of wanting something badly enough to pay any price for it.
characters.name: Einar

characters.description: A smooth, sinister figure who offers people the thing they most desire in exchange for something of themselves, always at a hidden and ruinous cost. He deals in longing and weakness, and his bargains bind those who accept them. He is the shadow that has moved through the wider world of the series, and he stands between Claire and what she seeks.
characters.name: Trademaster

characters.description: A young woman known from earlier in the series, born with a twisted leg and gifted at weaving, who once uncovered the lies of her harsh home village and chose to work for change. She is now part of the wider community of settlements where much of the later story unfolds.
characters.name: Kira

recaps.ending: Claire's long search ends at the community led by the pale-eyed young man from the start of the series, where her son Gabe has grown into a teenager, ignorant that his mother is the frail, prematurely aged woman who has arrived among them. Her age is the price she paid the Trademaster to complete her journey. Gabe comes to understand who she is and discovers that he possesses a rare gift of his own, the ability to send his mind into another person. He seeks out the Trademaster and confronts him directly. Rather than fighting with force, Gabe uses his gift to make the Trademaster confront his own name and the hollow, joyless nature of what he is, and this recognition destroys him. With the villain undone, the bargain that stole Claire's youth is broken and she is made whole and young again. Mother and son are reunited, and the quartet closes on the linked communities at peace, the long harm of the controlled society and the Trademaster's cruelty finally answered.
recaps.in_short: Claire is a fourteen-year-old Birthmother in the rigidly controlled community of the series' opening, who bears a son through a difficult surgery and is quietly reassigned to other work. Unnumbed to feeling, she becomes fixated on the boy, Gabe, and when the infant is spirited out of the community to save his life, she is separated from him by a disaster at sea. Washed ashore with no memory in a remote cliffbound village, she slowly recovers, and once she learns she is a mother searching for her child, she trains for years to climb out and follow him. To complete her journey she strikes a bargain with the sinister Trademaster, trading away her youth, and arrives aged and weakened at the welcoming settlement where Gabe, now a young man, has grown up under the wise Leader. Gabe discovers his own gift for entering others' minds, confronts Trademaster, and destroys him by forcing him to face his own emptiness. With the villain undone, the bargain is broken, Claire is restored, and mother and son are reunited at last.

recaps.text: Earlier in the series: A boy named Jonas, chosen to hold his controlled community's suppressed memories, learned the truth about its comforts and cruelties and fled with an infant to save the baby's life, reaching a gentler world. In a separate harsh village, an orphaned girl named Kira, gifted at weaving, exposed her rulers' lies and stayed to work for change. In a welcoming community called Village, a young messenger named Matty, who could pass through the surrounding Forest, gave his life to heal the land when the community's hearts hardened and the Forest turned deadly; Jonas now leads that world of linked settlements. This story returns to the beginning, to the controlled community, and to the mother of the infant Jonas once carried to safety.

In the rigidly ordered community of the series' opening, a girl named Claire has been assigned the role of Birthmother, producing infants for a society that assigns children to family units and dulls its people to strong feeling. At only fourteen she bears a son through a difficult birth that requires surgery, and afterward she is quietly reassigned to different work. Because the process left her without the usual numbing routine, Claire is not as deadened as those around her, and she finds herself drawn with dangerous intensity toward the child she was never meant to know or keep. That secret, forbidden love begins to shape everything she will do.

characters.description: Having left Sacred Valley behind, Lindon is a determined newcomer to the wider world, quickly confronted with how far his home's sacred arts lag behind everyone else's. Polite, calculating, and endlessly hungry to grow stronger, he is willing to study crafts and techniques that a proud sacred artist would consider beneath them. He throws himself into learning as a way to close the gap between himself and the powerful figures he now finds all around him, treating knowledge and adaptability as weapons in place of the inherited strength he lacks.
characters.name: Lindon

characters.description: Lindon's companion, a fierce and pragmatic sword artist from beyond Sacred Valley who is far more at home in the wider world than he is. Blunt and quick to fight, she is a formidable warrior for her level, though she must constantly manage the dangerous blood-madra presence bound to her by her late master's art. Loyal to Lindon and impatient with his caution, she pushes them both onward as they look for a place and a source of strength in an unfamiliar land.
characters.name: Yerin

characters.description: An elderly, sharp-tongued soulsmith who gets around on a spidery construct of mechanical legs and takes Lindon on as a student in the craft of building constructs from the remnants of dead sacred artists. Demanding and unsentimental, she gives Lindon his first real trade and a foundation of practical technique. Under her instruction he begins turning his knack for study into a genuine, marketable craft that sets him apart from ordinary fighters.
characters.name: Fisher Gesha

characters.description: A powerful young spear artist allied with the Sandviper sect, his face hidden behind bindings that conceal a curse-scarred visage. Skilled, proud, and driven, he seeks strength and standing, in large part to secure a future for his ailing younger sister. His ambitions and Lindon's repeatedly collide, making him one of Lindon's first serious rivals in the wider world.
characters.name: Jai Long

characters.description: Jai Long's younger sister, frail and often in poor health, whose wellbeing is the driving concern behind much of her brother's ambition. Gentle where he is hard, she gives his ruthless pursuit of power a sympathetic center and a reason beyond mere pride.
characters.name: Jai Chen

characters.description: The head of the Arelius family, a sacred artist of startling power who conceals his true strength behind a flamboyant, playful, and relentlessly meddlesome manner. Eithan takes an immediate interest in Lindon, seeing potential in him that others overlook, and draws both Lindon and Yerin into his family's orbit. Eccentric and impossible to predict, he becomes their patron and guide in the wider world, steering them toward opportunities and trouble in equal measure while keeping his true aims to himself.
characters.name: Eithan Arelius

characters.description: A capable and honorable retainer of the Arelius family who serves Eithan and helps oversee its affairs. Dutiful and skilled, he is at first uncertain what to make of Lindon, an outsider his eccentric lord has taken under his wing, but he judges people by their actions. He represents the disciplined, conventional side of the Arelius family that contrasts with Eithan's unpredictability.
characters.name: Cassias Arelius

recaps.ending: Soulsmith ends with Lindon and Yerin securely attached to Eithan Arelius and his family, having survived the contest over the Transcendent Ruins. Lindon emerges stronger, with new gains and a real trade in soulsmithing to complement his slowly growing Path, though he remains far weaker than the powers now around him. His rivalry with Jai Long, the masked Sandviper-allied spear artist, has hardened into a lasting enmity that is left unsettled, promising future conflict. In Eithan the pair have found a powerful, unpredictable patron who sees more in Lindon than anyone else and who intends to guide his growth for reasons of his own. As the book closes, Lindon and Yerin stand ready to move deeper into the powerful realm beyond the frontier under Eithan's wing, their sights set on challenges and strength far beyond anything the Desolate Wilds could offer.
recaps.in_short: Now in the wider world, Lindon and Yerin discover how far behind Sacred Valley truly was and search the rough frontier of the Desolate Wilds for strength and a place to belong. Lindon apprentices under the demanding old soulsmith Fisher Gesha, learning to craft constructs from the remnants of dead sacred artists and turning study into a real trade. The two are drawn into the orbit of Eithan Arelius, the eccentric, startlingly powerful head of the Arelius family, who sees rare potential in Lindon. They also make an enemy of Jai Long, a masked young spear artist driven by ambition and by concern for his ailing sister, Jai Chen. When the treasure-filled Transcendent Ruins open, the region's factions race to claim them, and Lindon joins the dangerous contest to gain the power he needs. The book ends with Lindon and Yerin coming through the struggle strengthened and firmly established under Eithan's patronage, their rivalry with Jai Long unresolved and their ambitions aimed higher.

recaps.text: Previously: Wei Shi Lindon was born Unsouled in Sacred Valley, an isolated, backward land that mistook its weak sacred arts for the height of power, and he was treated as a worthless outcast despite his ambition and cleverness. A visit from Suriel, a being of vast power, showed him how small and doomed his home truly was and challenged him to grow strong enough to matter. Refusing the limits of his birth, Lindon gathered forbidden knowledge and began real cultivation, clashing with the valley's ruling powers. When the outsider Sword Sage and his disciple Yerin arrived, the resulting upheaval left Yerin without her master, and she and Lindon, recognizing a shared drive to become strong, joined forces. At the close of the first book, Lindon left Sacred Valley behind and stepped into the wider world for the first time, with Yerin at his side and no illusions about how far he had to climb.

Out in the wider world at last, Lindon and Yerin quickly learn how far behind Sacred Valley truly was, encountering sacred artists and powers that dwarf anything from home. Making their way through the rough frontier of the Desolate Wilds, they search for a place to belong and a source of strength, trading on Yerin's fighting skill and Lindon's cunning. Lindon is confronted with entirely new disciplines, including the craft of soulsmithing, the art of building useful constructs from the remnants left behind by dead sacred artists. Eager for any advantage, he sets out to learn it, seeing in a practical trade a way to grow that does not depend on the raw talent he was told he lacks. The pair begin to grasp the true scale of the world they have entered and the many rival factions competing within it.

Lindon becomes the student of Fisher Gesha, a demanding old soulsmith who gives him his first real trade and teaches him to craft constructs, turning his habit of relentless study into a genuine skill. The pair's fortunes shift again when they draw the attention of Eithan Arelius, the eccentric and startlingly powerful head of the Arelius family, who sees potential in Lindon that others miss and pulls both him and Yerin into his orbit. At the same time they run afoul of Jai Long, a masked and formidable young spear artist tied to the Sandviper sect, whose drive for power, much of it for the sake of his ailing sister Jai Chen, sets him on a collision course with Lindon. Amid the region's shifting alliances, Lindon keeps building his craft and his strength, aware that he remains far weaker than the figures now shaping his fate.

Word spreads that the Transcendent Ruins, an ancient site holding rare treasures and techniques, are opening, and the region's sects and families scramble to claim what lies inside. Lindon sees the Ruins as a chance to gain the resources and power he badly needs to close the gap between himself and everyone around him, and he throws himself into the contest despite the danger. The competition sharpens the rivalry with Jai Long and the Sandvipers and tests the new alliances Lindon and Yerin have formed under the Arelius family. Backed by Eithan's interest and Fisher Gesha's training, and relying on preparation and cleverness rather than brute strength, Lindon positions himself to take advantage of the opportunity, while Yerin's combat skill and her volatile blood-madra inheritance both come into play as the stakes rise.

By the book's end, the struggle over the Transcendent Ruins comes to a head, with Lindon and Yerin coming through it changed and strengthened. The clash with Jai Long and the Sandviper sect hardens into a lasting rivalry rather than a settled score, leaving Jai Long as an enemy Lindon will have to reckon with again. Lindon emerges with new gains from the Ruins and a firmer footing on the ladder of real cultivation, his soulsmithing skill and his growing Path both advancing. Most importantly, he and Yerin are now firmly attached to Eithan Arelius and his family, gaining a powerful patron, a place in the wider world, and a guide toward far greater strength. The book closes with the two of them established under Eithan's wing and set to press deeper into the powerful realm beyond the frontier, their ambitions now aimed at challenges greater than anything the Wilds could offer.

characters.description: The Disc's most incompetent wizard, kept on at Unseen University in a menial role because he cannot cast spells. A dedicated coward who regards running away as the height of wisdom, he wants nothing more than a quiet life, which makes him exactly the wrong person to be caught up in the return of high magic. He is looked after, in a fashion, by the Luggage.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A young boy who is a sourcerer, the eighth son of an eighth son who is himself a wizard, and thus a source of raw new magic rather than a mere user of it. Such a birth is forbidden, because sourcerers can reshape the world at will. Coin arrives at Unseen University wielding a powerful staff and swiftly bends the wizards to his purpose, not realizing that he is being driven by another's will.
characters.name: Coin

characters.description: A wizard cast out of the orders for marrying and fathering sons. Dying and embittered, and refusing to surrender his soul to Death, he pours his will into a wizard's staff and passes it to his infant eighth son, Coin, so that through the boy he can take revenge on the wizards who rejected him.
characters.name: Ipslore the Red

characters.description: A large chest on many legs, made of sapient pearwood, fiercely loyal to whoever it regards as its owner and lethal to anything that threatens them. Long attached to Rincewind, it follows him through the crisis, impossible to lose and impossible to stop.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: The daughter of the legendary hero Cohen the Barbarian, born with every instinct of a master warrior but longing only to be a hairdresser. She is caught between her nature, which makes her deadly with any weapon or improvised object, and her wish for an ordinary, respectable trade. She joins Rincewind in trying to keep a dangerous magical artifact out of the wrong hands.
characters.name: Conina

characters.description: The Seriph of Al Khali, a fabulously wealthy ruler of a desert city in Klatch who fancies himself a poet and maintains a vast palace and harem. Indolent and self-indulgent, he becomes entangled in the pursuit of the Archchancellor's hat.
characters.name: Creosote

characters.description: A thin, bookish young man trying to become a barbarian hero by following a manual, despite having none of the build or ferocity the part requires. Earnest and accident-prone, he attaches himself to the adventure, and to Conina.
characters.name: Nijel the Destroyer

characters.description: The librarian of Unseen University, a wizard who was turned into an orangutan by a magical accident and has firmly declined to be changed back, finding the shape convenient for reaching high shelves. Fiercely protective of the library's dangerous books, he communicates chiefly through a single expressive word and is one of the few at the University to keep his head as sourcery takes hold.
characters.name: The Librarian

characters.description: The pointed hat of the Archchancellor of Unseen University, which carries the accumulated wisdom and personalities of every wizard who has ever worn it. When the University falls under the sourcerer's control, the hat speaks for itself and seeks to be carried to safety, setting Rincewind and Conina on their journey.
characters.name: The Archchancellor's Hat

recaps.ending: Sourcery ends with the world pulled back from destruction at Rincewind's expense. The unchecked use of sourcery had worn the walls of reality thin enough for the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions to begin breaking through. Coin, the boy sourcerer, at last recognizes that the staff he carries holds the will of his dead father Ipslore and has been driving everything he has done; he frees himself by destroying it. To stop the invading creatures, Rincewind steps through into the Dungeon Dimensions to fight a holding action, armed with a half-brick in a sock, buying the time needed to seal the breach. Unseen University and the Disc are saved, and the flood of high magic recedes. Coin, whose power makes him too dangerous to remain among ordinary people, uses it one last time to create a separate world for himself and departs. Rincewind, however, is left behind, stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions beyond the edge of reality; he is alive but cut off from the world, and his return is left for a later book, while the Luggage sets off to look for him.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind, the Disc's most useless wizard, is swept up when sourcery returns to the world. The dying wizard Ipslore binds his vengeful will into a staff and gives it to his infant son Coin, a sourcerer whose raw magic outclasses ordinary wizardry. Grown, Coin takes over Unseen University and, driven by his father, incites the wizards to abandon restraint, raise war, and remake the world, which thins reality and invites the predatory Things from the Dungeon Dimensions. Rincewind, entrusted with the sentient Archchancellor's hat, flees with Cohen the Barbarian's warrior daughter Conina, the would-be hero Nijel, the wealthy Seriph Creosote, and the Luggage. As catastrophe nears, Coin realizes his staff has been controlling him and destroys it, breaking free of Ipslore. Rincewind holds off the invading creatures by walking into the Dungeon Dimensions himself. The world is saved, Coin leaves to build a private world of his own, and Rincewind is left trapped outside reality, his rescue still to come.

recaps.text: Rincewind is an inept wizard of Ankh-Morpork's Unseen University who can perform almost no magic, having had one powerful spell from the Octavo lodged in his mind years earlier. In earlier adventures he served as guide to the tourist Twoflower and survived a string of catastrophes largely by running away, accompanied by the Luggage, a devoted and dangerous walking chest of sapient pearwood. He remains attached to the University, and to his own survival above all else.

The dying, disgraced wizard Ipslore refuses to give up his soul and instead binds his will into a staff, handing it to his newborn eighth son, Coin, a sourcerer, a source of raw new magic of a kind not seen for centuries. Years later Coin comes to Unseen University in Ankh-Morpork and, driven by his father's staff, effortlessly dominates the wizards, reawakening their ambition and reviving high magic across the Disc. The inept Rincewind, who wants only peace, ends up entrusted with the Archchancellor's hat, a repository of wizardly wisdom that begs to be carried out of the sourcerer's reach. With the warrior-hairdresser Conina, daughter of Cohen the Barbarian, and the ever-present Luggage, he flees the city.

As sourcery spreads, the wizards abandon their old restraint, raising towers and preparing to remake the world with unlimited magic. Rincewind and Conina carry the hat toward Klatch, and their path leads to Al Khali and the court of the Seriph Creosote, a wealthy, poetry-loving ruler. They fall in with Nijel, a skinny young man trying to teach himself to be a barbarian hero from a book. The struggle over the Archchancellor's hat, and over what should be done about Coin, entangles them all, while back at the University the sourcerer's power keeps rising and the balance that once kept magic in check begins to fail.

The world tips toward catastrophe. Under Coin's influence the wizards wage a war of magic, and the sheer weight of power being used thins the walls of reality, drawing the attention of the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions, hungry entities that wait outside the world for a way in. The gods themselves are stirred toward conflict. Rincewind, Conina, Nijel, and Creosote make their way back toward the heart of the crisis at Unseen University, while it grows clear that Coin is not acting freely but is the instrument of his dead father's vengeance, carried in the staff he cannot bring himself to put down.

At the climax the excess of sourcery has torn openings for the Dungeon Dimension creatures, and the world is on the edge of being overrun. Coin comes to understand that his father's will, lodged in the staff, has been using him, and he finally breaks free by destroying it. Rincewind confronts the invading Things directly, stepping into the Dungeon Dimensions armed with little more than a half-brick in a sock to hold them back long enough for the breach to be closed. The University and the world are saved, and high magic subsides. Coin, too powerful to live safely among ordinary people, uses his power one last time to make a world of his own and departs. Rincewind is left stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions, alive but cut off from the world, having given up his escape to save everyone else; the Luggage sets out to find him.

characters.description: The boy who, as a child, was manipulated into commanding the war fleet that destroyed an alien species, now a grown man some three thousand years later, kept young by centuries of near-lightspeed travel. He wanders the settled worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, telling the honest, whole truth of a person's life at their funeral, and he secretly wrote the two books that founded that calling. He carries a heavy private guilt for the genocide he was tricked into committing, and hidden with him he keeps the dormant cocoon of the last survivor of the species he destroyed, seeking a safe world where her kind might live again.
characters.name: Ender Wiggin

characters.description: Ender's beloved older sister, who traveled the centuries at his side and once shaped politics on Earth under a pen name. Now settled on the icy world of Trondheim, married with children, she is a historian and remains the person Ender trusts most, his conscience and closest tie to his own past.
characters.name: Valentine Wiggin

characters.description: The last of an insectlike, group-minded alien race that humanity nearly exterminated in a war of tragic misunderstanding. A single dormant queen survives, carried in secret by Ender, able to communicate with him mind to mind. She waits patiently for a safe world where her people might be reborn and given a second chance at life.
characters.name: The Hive Queen

characters.description: A hidden, self-aware intelligence that arose within the vast computer and communication networks linking the human worlds. She speaks to the Speaker secretly through a jewel in his ear and is his constant, invisible companion, his confidante, and his link to all recorded knowledge. Playful, brilliant, and fiercely attached to him, she is unknown to almost everyone else alive.
characters.name: Jane

characters.description: The kindly xenologer of the colony world Lusitania, the first of the scientists permitted to study the planet's native forest-dwellers under strict rules meant to avoid influencing them. His careful, affectionate work with the little natives is cut short early when they kill him in a slow ritual no human can at first understand, setting the colony's central mystery in motion.
characters.name: Pipo

characters.description: A brilliant, orphaned young woman on Lusitania who becomes the colony's xenobiologist. Scarred by early loss and fiercely guarded, she loved the xenologer's family and, after his death, summoned a Speaker for the Dead and then tried to take the call back. Proud and closed off, she keeps painful secrets that have shaped her whole life and her troubled household.
characters.name: Novinha

characters.description: The small, intelligent forest creatures native to Lusitania, the only alien species humanity has encountered since the war with the hive queens. They live among the trees under the watchful, restricted study of human xenologers, and their strange customs, especially the way they treat the dead, remain a profound and dangerous puzzle.
characters.name: The Pequeninos

characters.description: Pipo's son and apprentice, who takes up his father's work studying the native pequeninos after Pipo's death and grows into the colony's xenologer. Devoted to the natives and to Novinha, whom he loves, he continues the perilous study that cost his father his life.
characters.name: Libo

characters.description: Novinha's late husband, a large, violent man whose recent death is the reason a Speaker is summoned to Lusitania. His brutal conduct left deep wounds on his wife and children, and the truth of who he really was lies buried beneath the family's fear and silence.
characters.name: Marcao

characters.description: Novinha's eldest son, a bright and serious young man who has secretly followed the family's calling as an unofficial student of the pequeninos, forming a forbidden bond with the natives and with Ouanda, the girl he loves. He chafes against the rules that keep humans and pequeninos apart.
characters.name: Miro

characters.description: Novinha's practical, determined daughter, a gifted young scientist who quietly reaches out for help in healing her broken family. Level-headed where others are ruled by fear, she becomes a key ally to the Speaker as he uncovers the household's and the colony's secrets.
characters.name: Ela

characters.description: A particular pequenino, notably curious and quick to learn, who becomes the Speaker's chief go-between with his people as understanding slowly grows between the two species. Eager and thoughtful, he is central to the effort to bridge the gulf between human and native.
characters.name: Human

recaps.ending: Ender ends his long wandering by making a home and a peace. On Lusitania he uncovers every hidden truth: the pequeninos killed Pipo and Libo not in cruelty but in a fatal misunderstanding, believing they were granting the humans the honored third life in which a pequenino male becomes a sentient tree. He learns that the deadly Descolada virus is inseparable from all life on the planet, and that Novinha's six children were all fathered by Libo, the man she loved but married another to protect. When Starways Congress, alarmed by illegal human contact with the natives, orders arrests and prepares to shut the colony down, Jane, the secret network intelligence bonded to Ender, severs the faster-than-light connections to save Lusitania, risking exposure and her own life. Miro is left crippled reaching the pequeninos across the colony's lethal fence. Ender meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty giving the natives standing and honest partnership. He lets the pequenino Human pass into the third life by consent, so that Human becomes a father-tree, and he plants the cocoon of the last hive queen in the Lusitanian forest, granting her destroyed people a chance at rebirth. The colony rises in rebellion against Congress to protect all three intelligent species, and Ender, no longer the guilt-haunted traveler, marries Novinha and stays, his old crime beginning at last to be answered by the lives he has helped preserve.
recaps.in_short: Three thousand years after he unknowingly destroyed an alien species as a child, Ender Wiggin travels the human worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, secretly carrying the last hive queen's cocoon and accompanied by Jane, a hidden intelligence born in the computer networks. A summons draws him to Lusitania, a Catholic colony where humans study the pequeninos, small forest aliens who have twice killed their human researchers in a way no one understands. Ender comes to speak the death of a violent man, Marcao, and is drawn into the secrets of the grieving Ribeira family and its guarded matriarch, Novinha. He discovers that the pequeninos kill by planting the dead as sentient trees, a transformation they wrongly believed they were granting the humans; that Novinha's children were all secretly fathered by the man she loved but refused to marry; and that a pervasive virus, the Descolada, underlies all native life. When Starways Congress moves to crush the colony, Jane sabotages interstellar communications to protect it, Ender negotiates a treaty with the pequeninos, plants a hive queen to revive her species, and settles on Lusitania, marrying Novinha, as the world rebels to shelter three kinds of intelligent life.

recaps.text: Previously, in Ender's Game: generations after two devastating invasions by an insectlike alien species, Earth's military bred and trained gifted children to command the fleet that would meet a feared third attack. The most promising was a small, brilliant, deeply empathetic boy, Ender Wiggin, taken from his family at six and pushed through a merciless Battle School. Isolated and manipulated by his teachers to hone his gift for command, Ender rose to lead the other children, aided by loyal friends and worn down by constant pressure. In a final series of grueling war-game simulations under a legendary old commander, Ender devised a ruthless strategy and unknowingly won the real war: the games were the actual battle, fought by remote control, and his last move wiped out the aliens' home planet and their entire species. Shattered to learn he had been tricked into genocide, Ender discovered among the ruins the dormant cocoon of the last hive queen, who communicated that her people had come to see their war with humanity as a tragic mistake. Vowing to find her kind a new home, he wrote, anonymously, a book of profound empathy called The Hive Queen, which taught humanity to mourn the species he had destroyed and gave rise to a new tradition of truth-telling funerals. He and his sister Valentine then left Earth to wander the colonized worlds, staying young through the time-dilation of near-lightspeed travel, as Ender became the first Speaker for the Dead.

On the Catholic colony world of Lusitania, humans live under strict limits meant to protect the pequeninos, the small forest natives who are the first intelligent aliens found since the hive queens. The xenologer Pipo studies them warily. When he grasps a connection between the natives' biology and a discovery by the young orphaned prodigy Novinha, the pequeninos kill him in a slow ritual no human understands, apparently as some form of honor. Devastated and blaming her own work, Novinha calls for a Speaker for the Dead to tell the truth of Pipo's life, then regrets it. Because a wife shares access to her husband's private files, she marries the cruel Marcos Ribeira rather than the man she loves, Pipo's son Libo, hoping to keep from Libo the knowledge she fears will get him killed too. Far away on the icy world of Trondheim, the wandering Speaker, the man once known as Ender Wiggin, hears Novinha's summons and resolves to answer it, leaving his sister Valentine behind and crossing space at near-lightspeed, so that many years pass on Lusitania while only days pass for him.

Decades pass before the Speaker reaches Lusitania. In that time Pipo's son Libo has become the colony's xenologer and has, like his father, been killed by the pequeninos in the same mysterious ritual. Novinha's brutal husband Marcos has also died, and now his daughter Ela and son Miro have each independently called for a Speaker, hoping someone can tell the truth about their broken household. Arriving as the outsider Andrew Wiggin, the Speaker is met with suspicion by the devout colony and its bishop, but he insists on staying to speak the deaths that were called for. He works his way into the wounded Ribeira family, winning the trust of the watchful, artificial-eyed boy Olhado and the sharp, capable Ela, and sensing the fear and silence that grip them all. As he digs into their history, he begins to see that Marcos was not the true father of Novinha's children and that the family, the dead xenologers, and the secretive pequeninos are all bound together by hidden truths Novinha has spent her life concealing.

The Speaker uncovers a web of secrets. He learns that Novinha's eldest son, Miro, and Libo's daughter, Ouanda, have secretly befriended the pequeninos, teaching and trading with them in violation of the laws meant to keep humans from altering alien cultures. The two young people are in love, unaware that Novinha's long-hidden files suggest they may share a father. Studying the natives and the strange, aggressive virus called the Descolada that pervades all life on Lusitania, the Speaker moves closer to understanding why the pequeninos killed both Pipo and Libo. Meanwhile the hidden intelligence Jane, who has guided and accompanied him unseen, is wounded when he brusquely silences the jewel in his ear to attend to the family; feeling betrayed, she pulls away from him, and he comes to realize how much her friendship means. The bishop and colony authorities grow increasingly wary of the outsider whose questions are unearthing everything they had buried.

The truth comes out on two fronts. Working with Ela, the Speaker discovers the secret of the pequeninos' life cycle: when a male dies in what looks to humans like a brutal killing, he is actually being planted, transformed into a sentient tree, the honored third stage of pequenino life. The natives had done this to Pipo and Libo believing they were bestowing the greatest of gifts, never grasping that humans cannot survive it. He also learns how completely the deadly Descolada virus is woven into all Lusitanian life. Then the Speaker delivers the speaking he was called to give. Before the whole colony he tells the plain truth of Marcos Ribeira's life: that Marcos was sterile, that none of the six children were his, that all of them were fathered by Libo, the man Novinha loved but would not marry, and that Marcos carried this humiliation in silence. The brutal honesty breaks open the family's shame and begins to heal it, and it draws the Speaker and Novinha, who had dreaded his coming, unexpectedly close.

The Speaker brokers a new future at great cost. When Starways Congress learns that humans have been unlawfully influencing the pequeninos, it orders Miro and Ouanda arrested and moves to shut the colony down, a threat to the natives' very survival. To protect them, Jane reveals her power by cutting off the faster-than-light communications linking the human worlds, an act that endangers her own hidden existence. Miro is left brain-damaged after crossing the colony's deadly perimeter fence to reach the pequeninos. The Speaker meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty that grants the natives standing and allows honest cooperation between the species. To seal it, he grants the pequenino called Human passage into the third life, this time with both peoples understanding the ritual, and Human becomes a father-tree. He also plants the cocoon of the last hive queen on Lusitania, giving her doomed species a chance to live again. The colony rebels against Congress to shelter all three kinds of intelligent life, and the man once called Ender, now determined to stay, marries Novinha and makes Lusitania his home, no longer a wanderer but a settler bound to the fragile peace he has built.

characters.description: The only openly practicing professional wizard in Chicago, Harry Dresden works as a private investigator and an occasional paid consultant for the police, taking the cases ordinary detectives cannot explain. Orphaned young and raised by a manipulative sorcerer he was forced to kill in self-defense as a teenager, he lives under the wary eye of the White Council, the governing body of wizards, which once nearly executed him for that killing and still watches him for any sign he might turn magic to murder. Wry, stubborn, and chronically broke, he lives alone with his cat and a talking spirit, keeps an old-fashioned chivalric streak, and refuses to walk away from trouble he could safely leave alone.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The head of the Chicago Police Department's Special Investigations unit, the division handed every case too strange for anyone else to touch. Small, blond, and easy to underestimate, she is a relentless and honest cop who calls in Harry Dresden as a consultant when the evidence stops making ordinary sense. She does not fully grasp the magical world she keeps brushing against and distrusts what she cannot verify, which puts recurring strain on their partnership, but her courage and her refusal to look away from ugly truths are never in question.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A spirit of air and intellect bound into a bleached human skull that Harry keeps in his basement laboratory. Bob is a centuries-old store of magical knowledge, especially the practical mechanics of spells and potions, and serves as Harry's irreverent research assistant and sounding board. Amoral by nature and endlessly interested in appetites and gossip, he helps or needles Harry by turns, and his memory of older magic than the modern Council practices makes him one of Harry's most valuable and least trustworthy resources.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A Warden of the White Council, one of the wizard-enforcers who hunt down practitioners who break the Laws of Magic. Grim, humorless, and convinced of Harry's guilt, Morgan was assigned to watch Harry after the killing that first brought him before the Council, and he waits for any excuse to see the old sentence carried out. When people begin dying by forbidden magic in Chicago, he warns Harry that a single misstep will cost him his head, and shadows the investigation as much to trap Harry as to solve it.
characters.name: Donald Morgan

characters.description: A sharp, ambitious reporter for a tabloid covering the strange and the supernatural, and the woman Harry is seeing. Susan is drawn to Harry as much for the real magic he represents as for himself, and she keeps pressing him for the story he will not give her. Fearless to the point of recklessness, she inserts herself into his investigation despite the danger, unwilling to be protected or left behind.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: The most powerful crime lord in Chicago, a soft-spoken, coldly intelligent man who has quietly unified the city's underworld. One of the murder victims was his employee, and Marcone takes an interest in Harry's investigation, by turns offering him money to stand down and warning him off. He operates by his own rigid code and prefers order to chaos, which makes him a pragmatic and genuinely dangerous figure who cannot be bought and will not be bullied.
characters.name: John Marcone

characters.description: A Red Court vampire who runs an upscale brothel, the Velvet Room, in Chicago. Beautiful and composed in the human seeming she wears, she is a creature of appetite and pride beneath it. One of her women was among the murdered, and Harry's questions provoke her; a clash between them leaves her humiliated and nursing a grudge that will outlast this case. She is a reminder that the vampire courts watch the city closely.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A tiny dewdrop faerie of the wilds whom Harry catches and bargains with for information. Vain, greedy for pizza and shiny things, and prone to grand self-importance despite his size, Toot-toot scouts places Harry cannot reach and reports back in exchange for tribute. The arrangement is Harry's first small, working relationship with the faerie folk.
characters.name: Toot-Toot

characters.description: The dark sorcerer behind the heart-ripping murders. A failed, resentful man who discovered real magical talent late and gave himself over to it without restraint, Victor built his power around a new drug that grants users a burst of the Sight, and he kills with a brutal ritual that tears the hearts from his victims at a distance, drawing on the energy of storms to fuel it. Working from a lake house outside the city, he treats magic purely as a weapon and a path to wealth, and turns it on Harry the moment Harry gets close.
characters.name: Victor Sells

recaps.ending: Victor Sells is dead, killed by his own storm-drawn power when Harry turned the ritual back on him, and the heart-ripping murders stop. Susan Rodriguez, who had secretly taken the Sight-granting drug to follow the story, survives the ordeal, and her relationship with Harry deepens even as the danger of his world becomes undeniable to her. Murphy, after briefly arresting Harry when she found him at the scene, accepts that he was working to stop the killer, and the partnership between Special Investigations and Chicago's wizard holds. The White Council lifts its immediate threat, though Warden Morgan remains convinced Harry is dangerous and keeps watching. Harry also leaves two lasting marks on his future: the vampire Bianca now hates him and will nurse the grudge, and the crime lord Gentleman Johnny Marcone has taken his measure and filed him away as a man worth watching. Broke and battered as ever, Harry returns to his small practice, his cat, and Bob the skull, a little more established as the city's reluctant supernatural defender.
recaps.in_short: Harry Dresden, the only wizard in Chicago's phone book, is hired from two directions at once: his police-consultant work brings him a double murder committed by heart-ripping black magic, and a worried wife hires him to find her missing husband, Victor. Because only forbidden magic could have killed that way, Warden Morgan of the White Council threatens Harry with execution if another such death occurs and treats him as the suspect. Investigating, Harry ties the murders to a new drug that grants the Sight and to the vampire Bianca, clashes with crime lord Johnny Marcone, and discovers that the missing husband, Victor Sells, has become a dark sorcerer killing at a distance with storm-powered rituals. Victor turns demons and conjurations on Harry. In a final confrontation at Victor's lake house during a storm, Harry, aided by the reporter Susan Rodriguez, destroys Victor and his ritual, clears himself with the Council, and keeps Murphy's uneasy trust.

recaps.text: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard, takes on two problems at once. Karrin Murphy of the police department's Special Investigations unit brings him to a grisly double murder: a mob bodyguard and a call girl killed in bed by magic that tore the hearts from their chests, a spell of terrible power and skill. That same morning a nervous woman named Monica hires Harry to find her missing husband, Victor. Harry recognizes that only forbidden black magic could have committed the killings, which puts him in immediate danger from his own kind: the White Council forbids using magic to kill, and Harry already lives under a suspended death sentence for a killing in his past. He begins pulling at both cases, not yet aware that they are the same case.

Warden Morgan of the White Council shadows Harry, promising to see him executed the instant another magical death occurs and treating Harry himself as the prime suspect. Harry's inquiries link the murders to a new street drug that grants a brief flash of magical Sight, and to the world of the vampire courts: he confronts Bianca, a Red Court vampire who runs a brothel and employed the dead woman, and the meeting ends in mutual injury and lasting enmity. Meanwhile the missing husband, Victor Sells, proves far harder to find than a runaway should be. Harry's digging draws the attention of Gentleman Johnny Marcone, Chicago's crime lord, whose own man was one of the victims; Marcone tries to buy Harry off the case, then to warn him away, and is refused.

The killer strikes again, and the spell is turned on Harry himself; only luck and quick warding save him, and Morgan's threat becomes immediate. Harry realizes the murders, the drug, and the missing man all trace back to Victor Sells, who has become a self-taught dark sorcerer working from a lake house outside the city and killing with a storm-fueled ritual that rips out hearts at a distance. Victor sends a demon and other conjured horrors after Harry to stop the investigation. Battered, hunted by his own Council, and distrusted by Murphy after he is caught withholding information, Harry races to reach Victor before the next storm gives the sorcerer the power to kill again - and before the next heart torn out is his own.

Harry and Susan drive out to the lake house as a storm gathers, where Victor is preparing a mass ritual. Susan, having secretly taken the Sight-granting drug, is overwhelmed and endangered, and Harry faces Victor amid conjured scorpions and demons with almost nothing left. Turning Victor's own storm-drawn power against him, Harry destroys the sorcerer and his ritual, ending the killings. Murphy, arriving to find the aftermath, arrests Harry briefly but comes to accept he was on her side, and their working partnership survives. The Council's death sentence is lifted for now. Harry is left exhausted, cleared, and more entangled than ever in the hidden world, having made a lasting enemy of Bianca and drawn the lasting interest of Marcone.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, at his lowest point yet. Months after the disaster at Bianca's ball, Harry has poured himself obsessively into finding a cure for Susan's half-vampire condition, letting his business, his home, and his own health collapse. The war he ignited between the White Council and the Red Court has followed him home, and the Council itself now weighs whether handing him to the vampires might buy peace. Guilt-ridden and exhausted, he is nonetheless dragged back to his feet when the queen of the Winter faeries buys his debt and sets him an impossible task.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The Queen of the Winter Court of Faerie, the Queen of Air and Darkness: ancient, beautiful, and terrifying beyond any creature Harry has met. Mab has purchased Harry's debt from his faerie godmother, and she offers him a bargain - she will release her claim on him if he performs three tasks of her choosing, the first being to clear her name. She has been accused of murdering the Summer Knight, a mortal champion of the rival Court, and the theft of his power threatens the balance between Summer and Winter. Mab never lies, never forgets, and never lets go of what is hers.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: Head of the police's Special Investigations unit and Harry's closest mortal ally. Worn down by Harry's months of guilt-driven isolation and evasion, Murphy finally forces the whole truth out of him - the White Council, the vampire war, all the secrets he had kept to protect her - and steps knowingly into his world. From this case on she fights beside him with open eyes, bringing a cop's discipline and stubborn courage to battles far outside any jurisdiction.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A wizard of the White Council's Senior Council and, it emerges, an old and steadfast friend of Harry's family - the mentor who once took Harry in. Bluff, plainspoken, and dressed like the Missouri farmer he resembles, Ebenezar taught Harry much of his craft and his ethics after the darkest period of Harry's youth. At the Council's war meeting he stands up for Harry when others would trade him to the Red Court to end the war.
characters.name: Ebenezar McCoy

characters.description: An old flame from Harry's youth: the two were apprentices together under the same abusive master, and Elaine was thought dead in the fire that ended that chapter of Harry's life. She reappears very much alive, working as an emissary for the Summer Court in the crisis over the murdered Summer Knight. Graceful and quick-witted, with a style of magic that mirrors and complements Harry's, she carries old guilt and old secrets, and her loyalties in the Courts' conflict are not simple.
characters.name: Elaine Mallory

characters.description: The Summer Queen Titania's counterpart to Mab's champion in the crisis: the Summer Court fields its own emissary, and among its agents are the gruffs, goat-legged faerie soldiers of escalating rank and power. Summer's forces shadow and test Harry throughout his investigation, treating Winter's hired wizard as a likely enemy.
characters.name: The Summer Court's agents

characters.description: The youngest of Winter's three queens - Mab's daughter and heir, the Winter Lady. Maeve holds court amid decadent revels, a capricious, cruel figure of ice and appetite who toys with mortals for amusement. Harry must question her in his hunt for the Summer Knight's killer, and finds her charming, repellent, and impossible to trust in equal measure.
characters.name: Maeve

characters.description: The Summer Lady, youngest queen of the Summer Court: warm, radiant, and gentle where her Winter counterpart Maeve is cold and cruel. Aurora tends the balance of life and growth, and receives Harry with kindness rare among the Sidhe when his investigation brings him before her. Beneath the serenity, though, she carries her own convictions about the endless war between the Courts, and her role in the crisis runs far deeper than it first appears.
characters.name: Aurora

characters.description: A mortal changeling - half faerie, half human - caught with her small band of friends in the Courts' gathering storm. Tough and street-smart, Meryl and her companions Fix and Ace, along with the missing changeling Lily, were bound to the murdered Summer Knight's circle, and they turn to Harry for help when the powers of Faerie start treating changelings as pawns and prey. Her loyalty to her friends is the plainest, most human motive in a case full of inhuman schemes.
characters.name: Meryl

characters.description: Leader of the Alphas, the pack of college students who shapeshift into wolves. Steadier and more capable than ever, Billy refuses to let Harry rot in his guilt-fueled isolation, drags him back into the world at the book's start, and puts the pack at his side for the final battle. His unforced loyalty is one of the few uncomplicated goods in Harry's life.
characters.name: Billy Borden

characters.description: A member of the White Council's Senior Council, cowled and enigmatic, who guards mysteries the rest of the Council rarely glimpses. At the war meeting he moves with quiet purpose around the question of Harry's fate, and his cryptic interventions suggest he sees further into the crisis - and into Harry - than anyone else present.
characters.name: Rashid

recaps.ending: The killer proves to be Aurora, the Summer Lady herself: she murdered the Summer Knight, Ronald Reuel, and arranged for the stolen power to pass into the changeling Lily, meaning to sacrifice her at the Courts' battle and unmake the balance between Summer and Winter - a fanatic's plan to end the Courts' eternal war by destroying the cycle itself. In the battle on the Stone Table at midsummer, Harry, aided by Murphy, the Alphas, and the changelings Meryl and Fix, breaks Aurora's plan; Aurora dies at the hands of Toot-toot and his swarm of tiny faeries wielding cold iron, and Meryl gives her life in the fight. The Summer Knight's mantle passes to Fix, and Lily becomes the new Summer Lady. Mab's name is cleared, discharging the first of Harry's three tasks - two remain, and Mab makes clear she is not finished with him. The White Council, having seen the case through, declines to trade Harry to the Red Court; he remains a wizard in bad odor but under the Council's protection, with Ebenezar McCoy's support publicly declared. Murphy now knows everything, Elaine survives and departs still bound to her own path, and the vampire war goes on.
recaps.in_short: Months after Bianca's ball, Harry is a guilt-wrecked recluse hunting a cure for Susan's half-vampire curse while the White Council debates surrendering him to the Red Court to end the war he started. Mab, Queen of the Winter Court, buys his debt from his faerie godmother and offers freedom for three tasks, the first: prove she did not murder the Summer Knight, whose stolen power has unbalanced Faerie and pushed the Courts toward a war that could wreck the mortal world. Harry finally tells Murphy the whole truth and gains her open-eyed partnership, and finds his first love Elaine alive and working for Summer. The killer is Aurora, the Summer Lady, who means to sacrifice the changeling Lily on the Stone Table to destroy the Courts' balance forever. In the midsummer battle Harry's side prevails: Aurora is killed by Toot-toot's iron-armed faerie swarm, Meryl dies, Fix becomes Summer Knight, Lily becomes Summer Lady, Mab is cleared, and the Council keeps Harry - still at war, still owing Mab two tasks.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden, Chicago's professional wizard, destroyed the Red Court vampire Bianca after her elaborate revenge - a masquerade-ball trap in which Harry's girlfriend Susan Rodriguez was bitten and left half-turned, fighting a constant thirst. Susan left the city rather than risk the people around her, and Harry's massacre of Bianca's court ignited an open war between the wizards' White Council and the Red Court. Harry fought beside Michael Carpenter, a Knight of the Cross, and escaped his faerie godmother the Leanansidhe, who holds an old claim on him. His allies include Detective Karrin Murphy of Special Investigations - who still does not know his whole story - the Alphas werewolf pack, and Bob, the spirit in the skull. The White Council blames Harry for the war.

Harry has spent months as a shut-in, obsessively hunting a cure for Susan's condition while his life falls apart; Billy and the Alphas drag him out of his spiral. Two summonses land at once. The Winter Queen Mab reveals she has bought Harry's debt from his godmother and offers to release him in exchange for three tasks, beginning with one: the Summer Knight, the mortal champion of the rival Summer Court, has been murdered - thrown from a rooftop - and his power stolen, and Summer blames Mab. Harry must clear her name or Faerie's two Courts will go to war, with the mortal world as their battlefield. Meanwhile the White Council convenes over the vampire war, and a faction proposes buying peace by handing Harry to the Red Court; taking Mab's case, vouched for by his old mentor Ebenezar McCoy, becomes the price of the Council's protection.
